_comment: The KNOWN-BAD variant whose samples become the `negative_control` of the committed `klt yield` report (see sim/mc-yield.sh). Identical to the line campaign except that sim/mc-run.sh renders the deck with the campaign's `stat_scale` of 3, emitting one `.param` per statistical magnitude -- read out of the PINNED model libraries and tripled -- after the request's `.lib` cards, where ngspice's last-definition-wins rule makes them the operative values.

This is the defect `klt yield`'s negative control is specified against ('a mismatch seed pushed past spec'): the same circuit, same testbench, same window, a population three times as wide. `klt sim`'s own `monte_carlo.mismatch_scale` would do this in one field, but it is implemented for sky130 and gf180mcu only and refuses every other family, which is why the scale is built in the deck here (klayout-tools friction, see README.md).
n is 100 rather than 300: the control only has to be statistically distinguishable from the nominal population, which a 3x-wider population at 900 draws is by a wide margin.

PORTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, on the same terms as the item-5 grid requests (see sim/README.md): `models.pdk` selects the variant, every corner names its own PDK-relative section library (no `models.lib`, no generated corner bundle, no absolute host path), `options.osdi_preload` entries stay literal `$PDK_ROOT/...` so the fleet runner resolves them on its own box, and `options.stage_model_inputs` ships THIS host's pinned libraries and their whole include closure so the models that ran are bound by sha256 to sim/pdk.json's pin.
`netlist` is the deck sim/mc-run.sh generates under sim/build/ (gitignored); the runner substitutes an absolute path before submitting.

`options.keep_artifacts` is FALSE here and true on the item-5 grids: these campaigns expand to thousands of units, and a per-unit rawfile/log tree for them is neither committable nor useful. The per-sample seeds in the envelope are what makes a single unit reproducible.

`options.timeout_s` is 20 s, not the grids' 60 s. A unit of this deck takes about 1.5 s; 20 s is still more than ten times that, and the batch job ceiling is `timeout_s x units + 120 s <= 3600 s`, so 20 s is what lets `batch.max_units_per_job` be 170 instead of 58 and keeps the campaign to a handful of jobs rather than dozens.

`monte_carlo.vary` is `both` because the sections selected below drive BOTH kinds of variation and the bench does not get to choose: `cornerPNP.lib stat` and `cornerMOShv.lib mos_tt_stat` vary global `.param`s (one draw shared by every instance) while `cornerRES.lib res_stat` is re-evaluated per instance. Both facts are measured, not assumed -- sim/tools/stat_locality.py and sim/closed-loop-vref-mc/README.md.

`monte_carlo.seed_scope` is `point`, so a single point re-run or any re-partition of this grid draws the same samples as the whole campaign. `k_sigma` is 3 so the envelope itself reports the mean +/- 3 sigma window the spec row's `untrimmed line (3 sigma)` asks for; `vref_v` carries no `limits`, so that window is reported and can never fail the run.
